pass_a_gloss: on Pentecost. It typed worship of the law given through angels for one nation at the end of one feast, healing advancing in the last times and not continuing into what follows. He asks to wake desire for healing, not from ignorance. He calls God my Father alone and works by holding creation together—sun and heavens—and by making bodies grow. Equal to the Father he is Son as same substance; Arians who deny that equality are absurd and lawless. Dead means people once without faith called into life by faith in Christ; other living minds received life but cannot also give life. Those who do not come into judgment go either to Gehenna's fire as godless or to enjoyment of goods of true life, which is passage from death to life freed from Gehenna; middling lives stand on the right and on the left. Before the passion and resurrection, and even apart from baptism, receivers of Christ's word who trusted that he was the Father's Son were saved. Punctuate the text so he is judge as Son of God, not because he is Son of Man; the clause do not marvel answers those who saw a mere man while the speech was work for God alone. He said Son of Man above so they grasp him as both man and God: he judges as God and as a man tried in our diseases without sin who shares our weaknesses and forgives the rest. Or else: if I raise Lazarus do not marvel from that alone, for I will raise all the dead; those in the tombs means all who have died, including bodies consumed and never buried, who still count in the memorial number. Through fear and honor he pushes the human toward salvation; faith alone without good works does not save. He condescends again for unbelievers: nothing happens from him that the Father does not will,
pass_b_english: on Pentecost. This was a type of the legal worship given through angels to one nation only and at one time only—at the feast's end—that is, healing advancing at the last times and not continuing into what follows.
He asks not as one ignorant, but rousing him to desire to be healed.
"My Father," he says, "is mine alone and no one else's"; so by what with which he holds creation together—sun, heavens—and makes bodies grow, he works.
The one equal to the Father is especially called Son as consubstantial. Therefore the lawless Arians are laughable who deny that the Son is equal to the Father.
The dead are those once unbelieving and through faith in Christ called into life. Even if other rational animals received life, they cannot also give life.

Those who do not come into judgment are either sent into Gehenna's fire as godless and impious, or into enjoyment of unspeakable goods—that is, true life; for this is to pass from death to life, freed from Gehenna and counted worthy of divine honors. Those who lived in the middle stand "on the right" and "on the left" (Matthew 25:33).
Before the passion and resurrection, and apart from being baptized, those who received Christ's word and believed that he was the Father's Son were saved.

Punctuate it thus, and not as some think who, after adding "and he gave him authority to execute judgment," then add "because he is Son of Man" (John 5:27). That is not right; for he is not judge because he is Son of Man, but because he is Son of God—and for that reason he is also judge. He says "Do not marvel" (John 5:28) because to those who saw him he seemed a mere man, yet what was said was greater than a man and for God alone to do. He did not say that he is Son of God, but that he is Son of Man—this he had said above—so that they might understand him as both man and God. What he means is this: not only as God does he judge, but also as one who became man and was tried in all our diseases apart from sin, and as one who sympathizes with our weaknesses and forgives the rest. Or he says this: if I raise Lazarus, do not marvel at my power from that; for I am going to raise all the dead; "all who are in the tombs" (John 5:28) means all who have died. Since bodies consumed by beasts or fire or otherwise are not laid in tombs, yet they rise; for there will be a resurrection of all humans, and these too will be numbered among those in the memorials; for those who do good and evil are not the bodies in the tombs. So nothing prevents receiving also bodies consumed by fire or otherwise.
As you Jews, teaching and doing everything lawlessly by your own will—
Through both fear and honor, then, he urges the human being toward salvation. So faith alone is not enough to save unless one also has good works.
Again he uses condescension because of the unbelieving. That is: nothing happens from me that the Father does not will,
